title: Request stall detector and instance isolation windows for autoscaler stability
creator: Avery Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight on-instance request-stall detector that flags hosts exhibiting prolonged request stalls and places them into a short, soft isolation window. The goal is to reduce autoscaler thrashing and multi-region failover noise caused by intermittent long-tail stalls (KV cache stalls, slow kernel swaps, GPU contention) while preserving capacity and avoiding false-positive evictions.
background: We frequently see short-lived latency spikes on a subset of instances during regional failovers and heavy tail workloads. The autoscaler reacts to probe degradation and token-level latency signals, which in turn can cause aggressive scale-down/scale-up cycles. Existing readiness/liveness probes are binary and slow to reflect transient stalls; this causes oscillation and risks SLO violations across regions.
proposed_solution: 1) Implement a per-request stall detector that measures time-to-first-token and sustained CPU/GPU stalling heuristics for each served request. 2) If an instance exceeds configured stall thresholds (configurable per-route), mark it with a soft-isolation flag for a configurable isolation window (e.g., 30s-5m). 3) Expose the soft-isolation state via health metadata (readiness extras) so the autoscaler and routing plane can deprioritize the instance without removing it from the pool immediately. 4) Apply dampening to avoid repeated isolations (exponential backoff of isolation duration). 5) Integrate with existing circuit-breaker and regional failover logic: isolated instances are excluded from candidate set for regional evacuation and autoscaler scoring but still receive low-priority synthetic warmup traffic for healing. 6) Add observability dashboards and alerting to track isolation frequency, true-positive/false-positive rates, and SLO delta.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - False positives: healthy instances might be isolated during transient GC or scheduling events. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, dampening, and short initial isolation windows.
acceptance_criteria: New stall detector library in runtime with per-request TTF token and stall metric (unit tests + integration tests)
Soft-isolation state writable via readiness metadata and readable by autoscaler/routing service
Autoscaler scoring updated to deprioritize isolated instances (unit + canary)
No increase in client-visible 95/99 latencies after canary (<=1% regression tolerated), and overall reduction in autoscaler scale-churn by >=20% in chaos tests
Dashboards for isolation counts, average isolation duration, and per-region isolation rates
Playbook and runbook added for investigating isolation spikes with example queries and alert thresholds
rollout_plan: Dev canary: enable on a non-critical cluster with 1% traffic for 1 week
Staged rollout: increase to 10% traffic + synthetic chaos (network partitions / GPU pressure) and measure churn reduction
Regional rollouts: enable per-region with conservative thresholds, monitor for false positives
Global default: flip to enabled with production thresholds after 4 weeks of stable metrics
Post-rollout audit: 2-week review of isolation events and SLO impact
metrics: False-positive isolation rate (isolation followed by no degradation within 2 isolation windows)
